<lohna>, the noun form of the negative, and <hangin>, because of: placed after a verb, because of not doing or not being so; the clause that follows gives the result

terms: in order to pay off/to repay
definition: <loh>, pay off, with <nading>, written as one word: in order to pay a debt, as in {leibat lohnading}
the negative <loh> with <nading>, written as one word after a verb: for not doing, so that it is not done; usually written {loh nading}

terms: so as not to/in order not to
definition: the negative <loh> and <nadingin> written as one word after a verb: so that it does not happen

terms: so as not to/in order not to
definition: a short form of {loh nading}, written as one word after a verb: so that something does not happen; the same as <lohnading>
<loh> not, with <napi> although and the place marker <ah>: where or even though one has not done something
plural of <lohna> after a verb or describing word: the things that are not so, acts of not doing; {hoih lohnate} is things that are not good, wrongdoings
<loh>, not, and <ngal> written as one word after a verb, mostly <cih>: apart from doing or saying that, followed by a statement that there is nothing else
in {Lohon la}, one of the kinds of song sung at <Khuado>, named with {Dahpa la}, {Heisa la} and {Tuibung la}; apparently <lo>, field, with <hon>, group, the party that works the fields together
<lo>, field, with <hong>, guard, and the plural <te>: those who keep watch over a field
<loh>, not, with <pi>, placed after a verb: without doing it or although it was not done; it also names what was not done, as in {na theih lohpi}, what you do not know
<lohpi>, although not, with <pi> doubled for emphasis, after a verb: quite against what one wants, {ka duh lohpipi in} is although I did not want it at all

<lohsak>, pay a debt, with <zo> be able
negative <loh> with the plural <te>, after a verb: those that are not, the things not done or not approved; {hoih sak lohte} is things not found good, evil
the negative <loh> and <teh>, when, written as one word after a verb: when or because something is not done
<loh>, not, with <teng>, all, after a verb: all that one does not do, whatever is not; {na dawn lohteng} is all that you do not drink
the negative <loh> with the ending <un> used for a plural subject: without your doing; {na teltheih lohun}, in a way that you cannot understand

terms: be able to pay/be able to repay
definition: <loh>, pay, with <zawh>, the form of <zo>, be able, used before {kei leh}: {a lohzawh kei leh} is if he cannot pay

terms: be able to pay/be able to repay
definition: <loh>, pay, with <zo>, be able
capital of Kayah State in eastern Myanmar
<lo>, not, with the linking ending <in>, placed after a verb to join it to what follows: without doing, not doing but

terms: not one/not a one/no part/not a part/not a bit/not any
definition: used after {khat zong} or <kuamah> to say that not one of a group does something

terms: not at all/not a bit/not the slightest bit/in no way/to no extent/by no means any/not for a moment
definition: used after <bangmah> and a verb: without doing anything at all

terms: unaccompanied by/unescorted by/in the absence of
definition: used after <om>, be there: while someone or something is not present
grandmother of Timothy, remembered by Paul for her sincere faith
shake something strongly, or stir water; {lok gawp} is shake violently, make tremble
<lok>, shake, with <gawp> marking a thorough or violent action
get to pick or harvest a crop, with <kha> marking that the action comes about; negated in the verse: you will not harvest its fruit
particle prefixed to form nouns

work the land to grow crops, from <lo>, field, and <kho>, till; {lokho mi} is a farmer

<lokho>, farm, with <pa> for a man: a man who works the land
<lokho>, farm, with the plural <te>: those who work the land

of land: left uncultivated for a time; {lokhul-in omsak} is to let a field lie fallow
<lokhul>, a field left uncultivated, with <in>: lying fallow, as a waste field; {lokhulin omsak} is let lie fallow and {lokhulin bawl} is make into a wasteland
<lok>, shake, with the linking suffix <in>: shaking someone or something, as shaking a sleeper by the shoulder to wake him

terms: go to the field/work in the fields/farm

<lo>, field, with <kung>, plant: a plant growing in the field; {lokung hing} is a green plant
<lok>, shake, and <zo>, be able, written as one word: manage to shake or move a country, an army or the world
early in the morning or ahead of time, mostly of rising and setting out; {zingsang lol} is early in the morning
<lo> field with <lai> middle: the cultivated field, the open field; <lolai-ah> is in the field
<lolai>, the cultivated field, with the place marker <ah>: in the field
plural of <lolai>
<lo>, field, with <lam>, path: the path from the village to the fields, cleared before <Khuado> together with <singlam> and <tuilam>
<lo>, not, and <lua>, very, written as one word after a verb or describing word: not so much, or very much not
second half of the pair {innlum lolum}, house and home, all the shelter and living that a household has; it follows <innlum> and is not used alone
<lol>, early, and <zaw>, more, written as one word: earlier than the set time, mostly followed by <in>
a mass of something gathered into one: a lump of dough or clay, a lock or braid of hair, a pile
in the pair {a innma a loma}, her own house and her own field; <lo>, field, with an ending that the page does not explain
island of Indonesia, east of Bali
<lom>, gather into a bundle, with <cip>, tightly: gather something up and hold it fast, as the wind in the hands
<lom>, bundle, with <hen>, tie: tie things together in bundles, as weeds to be burned
<lom> heap or bundle with <in>; {a lom lomin}, heap upon heap
connective form of <lom>, pressing something together into a lump, as clay is shaped
<lom> bunch, lump, with <khat> one

<lom>, bundle, doubled, mostly as {a lomlom in}: group by group, many together
<lom> heap, doubled and with <in>: heap upon heap, in great numbers
<lom>, a lump or heap, with {-pi}, great: a large heap or the whole mass, as of dough, water, smoke or stones
of people or organisations, not a heap of things: a large body of people, or one of the large groups into which a whole is divided, then often followed by a number; {a lompi in} is in a mass

terms: in a column/in a thick mass
definition: said of smoke rising in one thick mass
plural; {a sia lomtangte} is the heaps of ruins
<lom>, a mass gathered into one, and <tat>, act, written as one word: do things together as one body
plural of <lom>: heaps, piles of things gathered together
<lo>, not, with {-na}: the state or place of not being or not doing; {a kilang lona-ah}, where it does not show, means in secret or aside

<lo> field with <nawl> edge
capital city of England and of the United Kingdom
<lo>, field, with <nei>, have: one who owns a field or vineyard; {lonei pa} is used of a man

placed after the word it excludes, mostly in a question or a negative sentence: except, apart from
young, newly sprouted grass or plants
plural of <longeek>
force something loose from the place where it is fixed and take it out, as nails, a window grille, a wheel or a plant with its root; the second part is <khia>, out
grassland where cattle feed; {lono etlawm} is the beauty of the pastures
grazing land, especially the open land around a town where its animals feed
plural of <lonona>: the grazing lands around a town
plural; the open land belonging to a town, said of the towns given to the Levites
hold and roll food in the mouth with the tongue
grass and other low green plants of the field; {lopa bangin}, like grass, is said of what soon withers
the negative <lo> and <pah>, at once, written as one word after a verb: does not, flatly or from the outset
<lopa> grass with <kung> stalk, plural
<lo>, field, and <pan>, from, written as one word: from the field
<lopa> grass with <no> young
plural of <lopa>: grass, the plants of the field; {gamlak lopate} is the grass of the field
the sowing of the fields; {lopawi hun} is sowing time

negative <lo> with emphatic <pi>, used as <lopi-in> or {lopi-a} after a verb: without doing, while not, before

<lo>, not, with <pi> and the plural ending <te>, after a verb phrase, those who are not or do not, as in {pasian ahi lopite}, those that are no gods
a joyful marking of an event such as a victory, a wedding, a festival or the installing of a leader; {gualzawh lopna} is a victory celebration
acting in a hurry without thought
a large motor vehicle that carries goods, often said together with <mawtawpi>
daughter of the prophet Hosea and Gomer; her name means not loved, not shown mercy
negative <lo> with causative <sak> after a verb: make someone not do or not be, as {lungkim losak} displease and {pau thei losak} make unable to speak
a firecracker, and fireworks of any kind set off at festivals
a kind of tax named together with <siah> and <mangmu>
<losap> with the plural <te>, those to whom a field, <lo>, is given out to work
a payment to the king, named after <siah> tax and <mangmu> in Ezra 4.20, where the English has taxes, tribute and duty
used in the pair <innsia losia>, ruined houses and fields, a heap of ruins
placed after the thing excepted: all but that one
pick what is left until nothing remains, said of gleaning a vine
throw something through the air or shoot an arrow; {suang lot khat} is a stone's throw
nephew of Abraham, who settled in Sodom and escaped when the city was destroyed
son of Seir the Horite and a Horite chief in the land of Edom
the negative <lo> and <tawh>, with, written as one word after a noun: without that thing, other than by it; after a describing word, with what is not so, as in {thuman lotawh}, by dishonest means
the parliament of Myanmar, its house of representatives; also written {Lutdaw}
negative <lo> with plural <te>, after a verb or adjective: those who are not, those who do not, those without
plural of <lo>; {leenggui lote} means vineyards

<lo> not with <teng>, all those: {bangmah tum loteng}, the things that amount to nothing

<lo>, field, with <thak>, new: a new plot cleared for farming, or new land to which people move to farm

<lot> shoot, with the plural <te>: the ones that are shot, as {ka thaltang lotte}, the arrows I shoot

device that makes the voice loud for a public announcement
a state in the south of the United States
city in Kentucky, United States, where a Zomi community lives
<lo>, farm or field, and <vai>, affair, written as one word; {innvai lovai} is the work of house and field
a gift of money given out of thanks to a preacher, singer or other servant of the church
<lo>, not, with the comparative <zaw>: more so not; {a gina lozaw}, less good, inferior; {kilawm lozaw}, even less fitting

the head of a person or an animal; {lu tung} is the top of the head

take over land or property as an heir or new owner; {a zi luah} means take over the wife of a dead brother
what is received as an heir or as an allotted share, especially land; of the Levites it is said that the Lord is their {luah}

connective form of <luah>, inheriting or taking possession; {za luah} is to succeed someone in office

<luah> possess with <khin>, which marks a completed action
<luah> possess with <kik>, again
what is inherited or possessed, especially land received as a share
<luahna> inheritance, with the plural <te>: the shares of land received
in {vut luahnate}, the tools for taking up ashes from the altar
<luah> possess with <pah>, at once
<luah> inherit with <pih>, together with someone
<luah> possess with <sa>, already: taken as a possession; {ka luahsa mite}, the people who are my inheritance

<luah>, inherit, with <to>, up: step up into the office, throne or position that another held
<lua>, vomit, with <huai>: making one feel sick, from a great height or from disgust
<luah>, occupy, and <zo>, manage to, written as one word: succeed in occupying a town or a position in war
a covered seat on which a person is carried
bear down on something with one's weight
of a tree weighed down with fruit

placed after a verb: keep on doing it and nothing more, just go along doing it without thought or aim
make something appear in the mind, with <mitkha>: {mitkha ah luaisak} is picture it in the mind's eye

form of <luang>, written {luan’} before <na> or <in>: {luan’na}, place where it flows
of water, a river, tears or blood: run along, flow
of tears, milk and honey or other liquid: run in a stream, pour down like a river
